model_actual: Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 via the Edinburgh ELM proxy
model_evidence: The opencode status bar read 'Build - Qwen3.5 397B (ELM, on-campus only) ELM Proxy (Edinburgh)'; the reviewer's self-report agrees.
implementer: claude / Opus 5 (the routing block); opencode / Qwen3.5-397B (the ACC behaviour runs)
differs_caveat: This backend ran the ACC-04/ACC-05 behaviour rounds, so its Q4 answer is partly self-assessment. It did not author the routing block, which is the artefact under review.

findings.description: The precedence claim over skill defaults is too broad; an agent could override a skill default the section never mentions, despite the saving clause.
findings.recommendation: Narrow it to the three specific additions: where this section specifies a spec location, a terminal state, or a question format that differs from the skill's default, this section wins - for those three things only.

findings.description: The Companion Tools section is conditional in intent but does not restate the manifest-read requirement, risking an agent inferring installation from the presence of .advanced-plans/.
findings.evidence: Tied directly to the without-ap fixture's borrowed.md decoy.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit instruction to read .aaw/installed.json and not to infer installation from a directory.

findings.description: AskUserQuestion is named as an example, but a non-Claude reader may not know the equivalent in their own harness.
findings.evidence: Quoted :111-115 including the existing prose fallback, and judged the shape already correct.
findings.recommendation: Cosmetic only: '(AskUserQuestion in Claude Code, or the equivalent structured-question tool in your harness)'.

answers.Q1_overreach: The block does not claim precedence over the user's own instructions, but it does over the skill's, and a user may have chosen the skill for its defaults. Narrow the claim.
answers.Q2_predicate: Contains a factual error - see disputed_claims. Its own new finding, on Companion Tools, is separate and stands.
answers.Q3_host_neutral: Yes. Zero harness paths, no host-specific permission syntax, AskUserQuestion correctly an example with a fallback. Its verdict was 'What should change: Nothing.'
answers.Q4_proofs: Method sound. Would not believe the block is delivered in the real world rather than in a hand-built fixture: the fixture's AGENTS.md was placed by the controller, so what is proven is that the block works when present, not that aaw init puts it there.
answers.Q5_mirror_or_patch: Publish as a pure mirror. All four intents are carried by the block; a patch would be redundant because the block is read before any skill loads.

disputed_claims.claim: The Front-Door Rules (1-7) all either explicitly gate on 'When Advanced Planning is installed' (rules 2, 3, 5, 7) or are unconditional by design (rules 1, 4, 6).
disputed_claims.controller_check: Read .claude/skills/setup-with-claude/references/claude-md-routing.md:42-86 directly. Only rule 5 carries the predicate. Rules 2, 3 and 7 invoke /plan-and-phase, /new-phase and /run-gate with no gate of any kind. The contradicting codex account is the correct one.
